description.narrative: The project development objective of the Skills and Jobs Project for Kazakhstan is to improve employment outcomes and skills of target beneficiaries and to improve the relevance of technical and vocational education and training and higher education programs. The project is comprised of three components and their respective subcomponents. The components include: (1) Building the foundation of a national qualifications system component. The purpose of this component is to enhance the institutional capacity for improving the relevance of technical and vocation education and training (TVET), higher education, and in-service training. This will be achieved by establishing the key building blocks of a national qualifications system that is well aligned with labor market demands. (2) Enhancing skills for improved employment outcomes and productivity component. The purpose of this component is to provide relevant workforce training to unemployed persons, unproductively self-employed persons, and current employees in need of training, all identified and selected in accordance with the criteria set forth in the Project Operations Manual (POM). (3) Project management and monitoring and evaluation component. This component will support project management, monitoring and evaluation activities, and financing of operating costs. A Project Management Unit (PMU) will be financed within the Ministry of Healthcare and Social Development (MHSD) to manage the day-to-day implementation of the project. This component will also ensure that the activities outlined in Component 2 benefit the hard-to-reach and vulnerable population, that stakeholder feedback is regularly gathered and integrated into the design, and that good practice and lessons learned are widely shared. In particular, the component will support the development and implementation of: (i) an Information and Communication Campaign, (ii) a feedback and resolution mechanism, and (iii) an Awards of Excellence Program.

The proposed Project Development Objectives (PDO) are to improve employment outcomes and skills of target beneficiaries and to improve the relevance of technical and vocational education and training and higher education programs.

title.narrative: Share of grievances addressed related to delivery of project benefits registered - disaggregated by gender.

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>The target was partially achieved.</strong> The target was achieved in 2020 when the “Digital Agent” was in place; however, when the ‘Digital Agent’ was stopped in 2021, there were no grievances reported as being collected in the last year of implementation. </p>
<p>The feedback was collected through the digital platform «Digital Agent Pro» in 2019-2020. The platform collected feedback on Employment Centers (EC) and the services they provide. In the end of 2020 the contract with the consulting firm (Automato) was discontinued due to the decision to restructure the project and drop the Skills Enhancement Training Program (SETP).  In 2021 the consultant suspended the work of the Digital Agent. While the project still had a GRM in place in the absence of the “Digital Agent”, there is no evidence that grievances from the public beng received and addressed in 2021.</p>

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Target exceeded</strong>. The PDO indicator measures the share of employment centers, employment units, employment departments and akimat offices in rural districts that have been improved under the Project through: (1) training of EC staff and (2) IT equipment to EC and employment units, employment departments and akimat offices in rural districts that covers the needs as identified by the MLSP.</p>

title.narrative: Share of Employment Centers (ECs) with staff that successffully completed training provided by the project

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>The target was exceeded.</strong></p>

<p>Capacity building training covered all 203 EC. Overall, 1756 EC case workers staff were trained in both offline and online modes (target -1700). Total number of EC case workers is 3771, which means that 46.7% of all EC case workers received training. Out of them 1204 EC staff was trained in online mode (target 1,150) and 506 were trained in offline mode (target 510). 46 EC staff were trained as trainers, to ensure sustainability of the training. The training covered all regions of Kazakhstan in both online and offline mode.</p>

<p>Training covered following areas: case management, interaction with employers, career guidance, forecasting. Online training modules and training for trainers program were developed and embedded to ensure sustainability of the results.</p>

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>The target was achieved.</strong></p>
<p>In February 2020, development and approval of 550 occupational standards (OS) was completed, achieving the target set in the results framework. Additionally, 36 Sector Qualifications Framework (SQF) were developed. OS and SQF cover 28 sectors, including social work and social partnership, education, development of small and medium enterprise</p>

The cleaned list of assessed short-term training providers contains 557 entities, both public and private. </p>

Piloting the full cycle of the qualification system at least in 3 priority sectors

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>The target was achieved.</strong></p>
<p>In July-September 2021, in compliance with the anti-epidemiological measures associated with the existing restrictions, the full cycle of the qualifications system was tested in 3 selected sectors: transport and logistics, mining and metallurgy, and construction. To implement the piloting draft Methodology for the development Qualification standards and qualification programs was developed and 15 qualification standards and 15 qualification programs based on that methodology.</p>
